text: 11-year-old girl. The patient has been experiencing a mildly pruritic rash on her trunk and extremities for 2 days. One week ago, she developed symptoms of low-grade fever, rhinorrhea, and headache. A facial rash appeared 4 days later, sparing the perioral area.

speaker: Doctor
text: Does the rash on her trunk and extremities appear blanchable, and have you noticed any swelling of her extremities or joint pain? I would also like to see a visual of the facial and body rash to check for characteristic features. REQUEST IMAGES

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Mildly pruritic rash on trunk and extremities. I also have Low-grade fever, Rhinorrhea, Headache, Facial rash not involving the perioral skin.

speaker: Doctor
text: Are there any raised, red cheeks or swollen hands and feet? I need to rule out erythema infectiosum.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant past medical history. Social history: Attends local school. Lives with parents and one younger sibling. No recent travel history.

speaker: Doctor

Do you recall any recent close contact with other children who had a "slapped cheek" rash or similar symptoms? Given the classic presentation of a facial rash sparing the perioral area followed by a body rash, this strongly suggests Erythema Infectiosum (Fifth Disease).

REQUEST TEST: Parvovirus B19 IgM

speaker: Doctor
text: The negative Parvovirus B19 IgM makes Fifth Disease unlikely, so we must consider other exanthematous illnesses. Does the rash have a lacy, reticular pattern, or are the lesions discrete maculopapules?
